title: Alan Dunne: Inside the Regime-Adaptive Portfolio

excerpts.label: 40-year disinflation regime ended
excerpts.insight: China, Soviet collapse, free trade, central bank independence all disinflationary—that confluence is over since 2020
excerpts.pm_takeaway: The macro tailwinds that made 60/40 work for 40 years have reversed—adjust SAA accordingly

excerpts.label: Hidden growth concentration
excerpts.insight: Typical institutional portfolio with 10-12 buckets may have 80-90% risk tied to growth and stable inflation
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Audit your portfolio by factor exposure, not asset labels—PE, VC, credit all correlate in drawdowns

excerpts.label: Debt levels 2x 1999
excerpts.insight: US debt/GDP double 1999; fiscal surplus then vs 6%+ deficit now—far more fragile backdrop for recession
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Next recession triggers step-change higher in debt; $40T household equity exposure = wealth effect fragility

excerpts.label: Trend following as midfielders
excerpts.insight: Trend following isn't just crisis alpha—it adds risk in uptrends, cuts in downtrends. Midfielders, not defense.
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Size trend allocation for regime flexibility, not just tail hedging—40% risk budget to adaptive

excerpts.label: Standalone vs total portfolio optimization
excerpts.insight: Optimizing hedge funds in isolation → market neutral; in portfolio context → macro, trend, commodities
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Behavioral bias explains underallocation to true diversifiers—take total portfolio view

excerpts.label: 1990s parallel is superficial
excerpts.insight: 90s productivity from PCs (supply-side); AI today is demand-side capex without proven productivity gains yet
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Don't extrapolate 90s equity returns—debt and valuation backdrop far worse now

excerpts.label: Adaptive portfolio compounding edge
excerpts.insight: Outperformance vs 60/40 since 1990 comes from lower drawdowns—compound from higher base after crises
excerpts.pm_takeaway: The math of avoiding 50% drawdowns beats chasing bull market returns—prioritize resilience
